name: Midges
note: Midges (docs 11, 12): not a creature with needs, arrival or trust but an ecology field, one share per square meter, that frogs eat (and later minnows, dragonflies and bats). field (S6a, the hourly tick): midges gather over still fresh water and the ground within nearWaterM of it, where plants feed them: each plant's weight (feed; a clump counts its size, a cover plant its share) is summed over a square of feedRadiusM, and fullFeed of it gives the most midges there can be. warmth scales that by season (spring, summer, autumn, winter). Each hour the field moves riseShare of the way up toward it, or fallShare of the way down, so a new reed bed fills with midges over a day or so and a drained one empties faster. A new world starts with none. When the journal first knows them is in recipes/world/journal.json (midges.seenAt). swarm (S6b-5): the live look, after Matt's pond tier 1 prototype but with no flocking: up to swarms.max swarms, apartM apart, on squares of this field holding at least fromShare of a full cloud: first up to overReeds over the reed clumps (midges dance over tall stems by the water), then the densest squares, equally dense ones in a seeded order so swarms spread over the island; a swarm of a full square holds perSwarm midges, times the time of day's share (density: dusk from duskFromH to duskToH hours after sunset, then night, then day, easing over an hour; fewer by windDamp in full wind; in rain they shelter in the plants, thinning from rain.thinFrom of the weather's rain and gone by rain.goneAt, and for afterH game hours after rain stops they come out up to afterBoost thicker, on the still damp evening); the quality tier caps the total (boids). Each midge loops around its swarm's centre at radiusM, heightM over the ground or water, speedHz turns a second (each drawn from the swarm's seed and its number, the same path in src/world/ecology/midge-paths.js and src/shaders/midge-draw.wgsl), and the centre bobs (bob, m and hz) and drifts up to windDriftM downwind. body: real size scaleReal, drawn readability times that (Matt, 2026-10-19: at real size no one could see a swarm from a few meters), albedo (linear), a forward-scatter glint against the sun (Henyey-Greenstein g, strength), at least minPx pixels wide (a smaller midge fades in step instead of shrinking); wingSheen: how much of the sky its beating wings mirror, so a swarm shows as pale flickering motes against dark reeds. dip: every everyS seconds one midge of a swarm dips to the water for s seconds and rings it.
_reveal: Coming back in the reveal on return (S7c, src/world/creatures/reveal-return.js): each swarm thickens back in over growS seconds, with no plop.

voice.note: The midge swarm's voice (doc 25 'Midges', model midge-swarm; src/audio/voices.js).json as its voice field (docs/audio-future-work.md). One voice per live swarm, at the swarm's centre, nearest swarms only (nearest). SOUND: a thin high hum of partials (a count picked per swarm in that range, mobileMax at most on the mobile tier) spread across hz (400 to 700 Hz), each detuned by up to detuneCents and wandering slowly by up to wander.cents over wander.periodS seconds (two slow sines per partial at unrelated rates), so they beat against each other; triangleShare of them are triangle waves, the rest sine. A soft lowpass at lowpassHz takes the edge off the triangles. tremolo is the faint shimmer of the wings (hz, depth). LEVEL: levelDb at full density; the hum follows the swarm's live density (0..1, from the ecology: dusk peak, night near zero, damped by wind) over rampS seconds. REACH: inverse distance from refDistance 0.5 m with a steep rolloff, and a hard fade from fadeFromM to reachM (about 3 m) so it is never heard in the far field: a player bending close to the water at dusk hears it, nobody else does. Distances are from the camera eye, so height counts. Tune by ear against a CC0 chironomid swarm recording if one is found.
